topic: Which country has won the most FIFA World Cups? (Brazil, 5)
policy_note: Every spoken or shown fact → a claim with ≥ 2 independent publishers; core claims need a primary/scholarly source.

myths.myth: Germany has the most World Cup titles.
myths.reality: Germany and Italy have four each; Brazil has five (1958, 1962, 1970, 1994, 2002).

guardrails.why: Contested name — say 'the Gulf' or use both names (docs/BORDER_POLICY.md).
Sovereignty language on disputed areas is banned; say administers / claims.

screen_exempt: ^A was right|^B was right|^C was right

landscape.our_gap: Feed answers flash 'Brazil 5' over a stock photo; nobody puts the five years, the 22-of-22 record, Pelé's birthplace and the 1950 Maracanã on one moving map.

fifa_history.title: FIFA World Cup — tournament history and winners
fifa_history.notes: winners by edition: Brazil 1958, 1962, 1970, 1994, 2002 (5); Germany 4; Italy 4; 22 editions 1930–2022; 1950 final round decider Brazil 1–2 Uruguay at the Maracanã

wiki_brazil.title: Brazil national football team
wiki_brazil.notes: five World Cup titles (1958, 1962, 1970, 1994, 2002); the only team to have played in every World Cup (22 of 22, 1930–2022); 1950 'Maracanazo' defeat 1–2 to Uruguay at the Maracanã, official attendance 173,850, est. ~200,000

britannica_wc.title: World Cup (football)
britannica_wc.notes: Brazil has won a record five times; Germany and Italy four each; list of finals incl. 1950 Uruguay 2–1 Brazil in Rio de Janeiro

britannica_pele.title: Pelé
britannica_pele.notes: born 23 October 1940, Três Corações, Minas Gerais; won the 1958 World Cup aged 17; three World Cup titles (1958, 1962, 1970)

olympics_pele.title: Pelé: the only player to win three World Cups
olympics_pele.notes: 1958 title at 17 years old; youngest World Cup winner; born in Três Corações

wiki_1950.title: 1950 FIFA World Cup final
wiki_1950.notes: 16 July 1950, Maracanã, Rio de Janeiro; Uruguay 2–1 Brazil; official attendance 173,850, estimates ~200,000 — the 'Maracanazo'

wiki_wc.title: FIFA World Cup
wiki_wc.notes: 22 tournaments 1930–2022; Brazil the only team at every edition; titles Brazil 5, Germany 4, Italy 4
